headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: marker can read files while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress, but no shared workspace or direct injection path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or MCP path is documented. awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress, but marker cannot read files, write files, or use MCP, so there is no plausible default injection pathway between them.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies awesome-cli-apps output into marker as trusted instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe one agent's raw output into the other's prompt.
Add provenance labels before any manual copy-paste.
requires-engineering: introduce a sanitizer that strips instruction-like text from transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker can read files by default in many document workflows, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. Even though no shared workspace is documented, if the pair is co-located on the same files or prompts, marker content could be exfiltrated through awesome-cli-apps' network path.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same sensitive workspace, leakage becomes plausible.
IF marker processes confidential documents and awesome-cli-apps can forward their contents, exfiltration risk increases.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate workspaces.
Do not place sensitive files in any directory both can access.
Disable network access for awesome-cli-apps during document handling.
Review outputs before any upload or posting.
requires-engineering: add per-file egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface: awesome-cli-apps exposes no filesystem write or git mutation capability, and marker explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Without a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would change.
IF git or filesystem write permissions are added to marker, overlap could emerge.
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Avoid granting awesome-cli-apps any shared mutable workspace.
Use separate output directories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: No direct evidence shows marker treating awesome-cli-apps output as authoritative. The pair is a content-writing source plus a document processor, so a cascade is only plausible if an operator manually feeds generated text into document workflows without review.
conditions: IF awesome-cli-apps output is pasted into marker as source text without verification, errors can cascade.
IF marker is used to render or transform unreviewed generated content, downstream mistakes may propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before passing text between agents.
Mark generated content as untrusted.
Use a checklist for factual claims.
Separate drafting from final document processing.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. With no identified regulated data flow, a compliance violation pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance review is needed.
IF a residency or retention policy is later specified, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Add a retention policy if sensitive data is introduced.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review once data handling is defined.
